security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives from markdown fences, sample URLs, timestamps, and checklist text rather than executable behavior. Add safety notes for target cluster checks, read-only defaults, and human confirmation before any production command is used.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Operational Command in Template
semantic_findings.description: The quick reference includes `redis-cli FLUSHDB` as an emergency cache clear command. If copied into a live environment without scoping, it can delete Redis data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command appears directly in the operational quick reference, and FLUSHDB is a destructive Redis action. It is documentation rather than auto-execution, so the risk is user or agent misuse.

content.value_statement: On-call shifts lose context when incidents, changes, and risks are scattered. This skill provides structured handoff templates, checklists, and escalation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Provides complete shift handoff templates for active incidents, investigations, recent changes, and upcoming events.
Offers a quick async handoff format for short shift transitions.
Includes a mid-incident handoff structure for current state, actions taken, and next steps.
Defines pre-shift, daily, and post-shift checklists for on-call engineers.
Gives escalation triggers and guidance for clean context transfer.
limitations: It does not connect to monitoring, ticketing, chat, or paging systems.
It cannot verify production access, alert routing, or incident status.
Examples use placeholder services and links that teams must replace.
Command examples require human review before use in any environment.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Shift Change
use_cases.description: Create a handoff that captures incidents, investigations, recent changes, known issues, and upcoming events.

use_cases.title: Transfer a Live Incident
use_cases.description: Summarize current state, mitigation progress, next actions, owners, and communication status during an incident.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Process
use_cases.description: Build repeatable handoff routines with overlap timing, checklists, escalation triggers, and documentation expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an on-call handoff for my shift. Ask me for active incidents, ongoing investigations, recent changes, known issues, and upcoming events.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Async Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these notes into a concise async handoff for the incoming on-call engineer: [paste notes]. Highlight watch items and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Structure a Mid-Incident Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mid-incident handoff for this active incident: [paste incident details]. Include current state, actions taken, next steps, owners, and escalation path.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Team Handoff Process
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this current on-call handoff process: [paste process]. Identify gaps, add checklists, define timing, and suggest escalation improvements.

output_examples.input: I have one active payment incident, a memory investigation, and a release tomorrow.
output: Active incident summary with severity, impact, mitigation, and owner.
Watch list for the memory investigation with next checks.
Upcoming release note with monitoring and escalation guidance.

output_examples.input: Our team needs a repeatable handoff process for weekly rotations.
output_examples.output: A structured process with a 30 minute overlap, outgoing and incoming responsibilities, required sections, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Payment errors are improving after scaling pods, but the cause is still unknown.
output_examples.output: A mid-incident transfer that records current error rate, actions taken, remaining hypotheses, next decision points, and escalation contacts.

best_practices: Keep handoffs focused on active risk, recent changes, next actions, and escalation paths.
Use a short synchronous review for active incidents or complex investigations.
Replace placeholder links, contacts, and service names with current team-owned references.
anti_patterns: Do not hand off only through chat history when an incident is active.
Do not include commands without environment, approval, and rollback context.
Do not omit known issues, failed mitigations, or unresolved questions.

faq.question: Can this skill create a full on-call handoff document?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides templates for shift summaries, active incidents, investigations, recent changes, and escalation reminders.

faq.question: Does it integrate with PagerDuty, Slack, Grafana, or ticketing tools?
faq.answer: No. It gives documentation patterns and placeholder links only. Teams must add their own systems.

faq.question: Can it be used during an active incident?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a mid-incident handoff format for state, mitigation, owners, next steps, and communication status.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: On-call engineers, incident commanders, SRE leads, and DevOps teams can use it to reduce context loss.

faq.question: Does it execute operational commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation only. Any command examples require human review before execution.

faq.question: How should teams adapt the templates?
faq.answer: Replace sample services, links, contacts, severity labels, and escalation paths with team-approved references.
